title: The Renown SDK provides DID-based authentication using did:pkh, with hook-based init, cookie sessions, and profile enrichment
content:
The `@renown/sdk` provides decentralized identity authentication for Powerhouse apps. There is **no provider component**: `RenownUserProvider` returns zero hits in source. Initialization runs through the `useRenownInit` hook (`packages/reactor-browser/src/hooks/renown.ts`), and no `window.renown` / `window.connectCrypto` globals exist. `useUser()` returns `User | undefined` (`renown.ts:29`) -- not an object bundle; the other values come from sibling hooks (`useRenown`, `useLoginStatus`, `useRenownLoginMethods`, `useRenownInitialUser`). Users are identified by DIDs in `did:pkh:eip155:<chainId>:<ethAddress>` format. The `User` type includes `did`, `address`, `name`, `email`, `avatar`, and `ethAddress`. Sessions are **not** in `sessionStorage` -- that identifier has zero hits in the entire monorepo. The session lives in a cookie, `RENOWN_SESSION_COOKIE = "renown_session"` (`packages/renown/src/constants.ts:6`), with a localStorage seed used only to cover the first paint before the SDK becomes authoritative. The `RenownAuthButton` is a headless component with render props for customization. LoginStatus flows: `initial` -> `checking` -> `authorized` | `not-authorized`.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._
description: No provider component: init is via useRenownInit. useUser() returns User|undefined. Sessions live in the renown_session cookie, not sessionStorage.
